chip_grid_axes_note: the two ground axes of a burst are perpendicular: the range axis is reported as a line (mod 180°), the azimuth axis is that line rotated by 90°, and which of the two perpendicular senses is the flight direction follows from the orbit direction reported per chip in ywf_bursts.json
note: this anchor supports a statement about *where the tower stood and which road it fell on*, not a band/edge layer: such a layer needs a resolvable ground extent per pixel along the band axis, and ``road_vs_pixel_grid`` is the number that says how far this record is from that

road.anchor: carriageway centreline of the OSM way — never an area/polygon (the Bergsøysund analysis measured a −81..+7 m shape error, rms 56 m, for a polygon anchor)
road.carriageway_width_source: assumption, not a survey: the way carries no width tag; a two-lane carriageway is taken as 7.0 m

road_vs_window.note: the road lies outside the frame: the near carriageway edge is 8.10-9.33 px across range from the window centre, while a 7x7 frame reaches 6 px at most (3 px from its centre), so no committed pixel crosses the carriageway - and a frame that did contain it would still have to resolve the 7.0 m cross-section (1.71-1.96 px across range, 0.13-0.26 px across azimuth). Containment needs 19-21 px per side (27-29 px with Bautzen's +/-4-row ROI): a frame of 19 px per side is 361 samples (7.4x the committed 49 px) and 29 px per side 841 (17.2x) — the cost of containment is quadratic in the side, and this is the containment half of blocker 4 of code/ywf/README.md

status: anchor reference — no edge layer is claimed: a 7x7 window per acquisition, no rect/pixel-spacing spec and no per-section coordinates (see code/ywf/README.md)

window.note: one 7x7 complex window per acquisition at the asset point; the export committed no per-section coordinates (its segment_latitude / segment_longitude columns are empty for all five mast sections), so this package has no second anchor and no rect spec
